top_choice_rationale: Mircea Cărtărescu (P001) is the only awardable proposal, and I judge him worthy on the common criteria. He has a voice recognisable at paragraph level, and he builds memory, the body, dream and cosmology into a recursive, densely patterned prose architecture. He has sustained that project over decades in very large books, chiefly the Blinding (Orbitor) trilogy and Solenoid. On public knowledge, Solenoid poses a different formal and metaphysical problem from the earlier trilogy, which points to development rather than repetition, but I have not verified this against the Romanian text. The citation is cleanly attributable to one writer in one language. Its weight should rest on the major prose, with the poetry named as its lyric root, since translated coverage of the poetry and early work is uneven. The main uncertainty is how much of the Romanian rhythm, wordplay and syntax survives in translation. Neither I nor, as far as I know, my colleagues can judge that directly, and a Romanian-language assessment would be the right test. I do not count the unanimous opening rankings as evidence. P000 ranks second: the translation and repetition reservations are real but do not outweigh the evidence of distinctive voice, formal ambition and sustained depth, so I prefer an award to no award.
recusal_note: none apparent from the supplied profile; no documented tie to Cărtărescu or any shortlisted writer. My own work as a novelist, short-story writer and Lagerlöf biographer is context, not evidence of preference.
